response: As I sit alone on my birthday, surrounded by the familiar comforts of my childhood home, I'm struck by the realization that I've spent my entire life carrying the weight of family expectations on my shoulders. (As an only child, I've had to navigate the complexities of family dynamics without the distraction of siblings, and this has often led to a deep sense of responsibility and self-reliance.) Growing up, I've always felt like I was the default parent, the one who had to take care of my parents' needs and manage the household on my own. (This has taught me to be resourceful and independent, but it's also left me with a lingering sense of guilt and obligation.) As I've grown older, I've come to realize that this dynamic has shaped my approach to relationships and challenges in profound ways. (For example, I've often found myself taking on a caretaking role in my adult relationships, trying to anticipate and meet the needs of those around me.) But it's also led me to a deeper understanding of the importance of setting boundaries and prioritizing my own needs. (As I've learned to let go of the need to be the sole provider and caregiver, I've discovered a sense of freedom and autonomy that I never knew was possible.) And yet, even as I've grown more confident in my ability to navigate life's challenges on my own, I still feel the weight of family expectations bearing down on me. (It's a strange and complex feeling, one that I'm still trying to untangle and understand.)
